topic.label: Energy Science and Engineering
topic.desc: Energy Science and Engineering: converting, storing, delivering and managing energy, and assessing its economic and environmental impact.

concepts: Laws of thermodynamics applied to power cycles, heat engines, heat pumps and efficiency limits.
Solar, wind, hydro and geothermal resources, their variability and the technologies that harvest them.
Batteries, fuel cells, hydrogen and other storage technologies and their performance and degradation.
Transmission, distribution, dispatch and integrating variable renewables while keeping the grid reliable.
Fossil, bio and nuclear fuels, combustion chemistry, emissions and reactor fundamentals.
Energy Systems Analysis, Economics and Policy
Life cycle assessment, levelized cost, decarbonization pathways and the policy that shapes energy transitions.
skills: Computes efficiency and work of Rankine, Brayton and combined cycles and checks energy balance closure.
Sizes heat pumps from load and climate data and checks coefficient of performance across temperatures.
Locates exergy destruction in a process and checks totals against first and second law balances.
Estimates photovoltaic energy yield from irradiance and system design and checks losses and capacity factor.
Fits wind speed distributions and turbine power curves and checks annual energy against measured data.
Screens candidate sites by resource, land and grid access and checks layers with spatial data.
Sizes battery storage for a load and duty cycle and checks depth of discharge and degradation limits.
Compares electrochemical storage chemistries by energy density, cost and lifetime and checks figures against literature.
Solves unit commitment and dispatch problems and checks constraint satisfaction and marginal prices.
Assesses hosting capacity and curtailment for added renewables and checks frequency and voltage limits.
Designs microgrids with generation, storage and controls and checks reliability under outage scenarios.
Computes stoichiometry, adiabatic flame temperature and emissions and checks mass balance.
Explains reactor physics, fuel cycles and safety systems and checks claims against technical references.
Computes levelized cost of energy with discounting and checks sensitivity to capital cost and capacity factor.
Performs life cycle carbon accounting for an energy technology and checks system boundaries and inventory data.
Evaluates energy transition scenarios against emissions targets and checks assumptions with cited data.
